extracted.intended_audience: NSF proposers (PIs), authorized organization representatives (AORs), proposal administrators, external reviewers, and NSF program staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for processing, reviewing, and deciding NSF proposals per PAPPG Chapter III, including merit review principles and criteria, reviewer selection, proposal file updates, revisions during review, funding recommendation, award decision, appeal procedures, and disclosure of review materials and proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Principles — highest quality and potential to advance knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: All NSF projects should be of the highest quality and have the potential to advance, if not transform, the frontiers of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles are to be given due diligence by PIs and organizations when preparing proposals and managing projects, by reviewers when reading and evaluating proposals, and by NSF program staff when determining recommendations and overseeing awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Principles — contribution to societal goals (Broader Impacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF projects, in the aggregate, should contribute more broadly to achieving societal goals. These broader impacts may be accomplished through the research itself, through activities that are directly related to specific research projects, or through activities that are supported by, but are complementary to, the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project activities may be based on previously established and/or innovative methods and approaches, but in either case must be well justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Principles — meaningful assessment and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaningful assessment and evaluation of NSF funded projects should be based on appropriate metrics, keeping in mind the likely correlation between the effect of broader impacts and the resources provided to implement projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If activity size is limited, evaluation in isolation may not be meaningful; assessment may be best at a higher aggregated level. PIs are expected to be accountable: projects should include clearly stated goals, specific descriptions of activities, and a plan to document outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criterion — Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Intellectual Merit criterion encompasses the potential to advance knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion is one of two NSB-approved merit review criteria and must be given full consideration; it is necessary but not sufficient by itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criterion — Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Broader Impacts criterion encompasses the potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion is one of two NSB-approved merit review criteria and must be given full consideration; it is necessary but not sufficient by itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements to consider in review — potential to advance knowledge / benefit society
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the potential for the proposed activity to: Advance knowledge and understanding within its own field or across different fields (Intellectual Merit); and Benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes (Broader Impacts)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should weigh these potential outcomes when evaluating both Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements to consider in review — creativity and transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do the proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original, or potentially transformative concepts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider novelty and transformative scope as part of overall assessment for both criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements to consider in review — plan quality and assessment mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the plan for carrying out the proposed activities well-reasoned, well-organized, and based on a sound rationale? Does the plan incorporate a mechanism to assess success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to technical aspects and to activities intended to achieve Broader Impacts; inclusion of success metrics and assessment methods is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements to consider in review — qualifications of individuals/team/organization
rubrics_metrics.description: How well qualified is the individual, team, or organization to conduct the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate experience, expertise, and prior accomplishments relevant to the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements to consider in review — adequacy of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there adequate resources available to the PI (either at the home organization or through collaborations) to carry out the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional support, facilities, collaborations, and other resources when judging feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Reviewers — special knowledge of subfields
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimally, reviewers should have special knowledge of the science and engineering subfields involved in the proposals to be reviewed to evaluate competence, intellectual merit, and utility of the proposed activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within reasonable limits, reviewers’ fields of specialty should be complementary within a reviewer group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Reviewers — broader/generalized expertise for broader impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should have broader or more generalized knowledge of the science and engineering subfields involved to evaluate the broader impacts of the proposed activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers with broad expertise are required for proposals involving substantial size or complexity, broad disciplinary or multidisciplinary content, or significant national or international implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Reviewers — knowledge of infrastructure and educational activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should have broad knowledge of the infrastructure of the science and engineering enterprise, and its educational activities, to evaluate contributions to societal goals, scientific and engineering personnel, and distribution of resources to organizations and geographical areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Reviewers — diverse representation
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent possible, diverse representation within the review group is sought to achieve a balance among various characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important factors include type of organization represented, reviewer diversity, age distribution and geographic balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal File Updates — who may request and required justification
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a proposal file update must be signed and submitted by the AOR. A Proposal Update Justification must address why the changes or file replacements are being requested and any differences between the original and proposed replacement files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Submitted Proposals Module in Research.gov; authorized individuals in the organization’s SPO can initiate or review requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal File Updates — timing and automatic acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a proposal file update will be automatically accepted if submitted prior to: the deadline date; initiation of external peer review in cases when a target date is utilized; and initiation of external peer review in the case of an unsolicited proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests after these timeframes require acceptance by the cognizant NSF Program Officer and should be limited to correcting technical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal File Updates — restrictions after deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a proposal file update after the specified timeframes will require acceptance by the cognizant NSF Program Officer and shall be submitted only to correct a technical problem (i.e., formatting or print problems). Changes in the content of the proposal should not be requested after the timeframes specified above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When accepted, replacement files immediately replace existing files and become part of the official proposal. NSF will consider only one request per proposal at a time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions during review — notification of significant developments
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a significant development that might materially affect the outcome of the review of a pending proposal, the proposer must contact the cognizant NSF Program Officer to discuss the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting additional information must not be used to circumvent page limitations or stated deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget negotiation constraints during award discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: The cognizant NSF Program Officer may suggest reducing or eliminating costs for specific budget items that are clearly unnecessary or unreasonable, and may discuss the 'bottom line' award amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generally does not include faculty salaries, salary rates, fringe benefits, or tuition. Indirect cost (F&A) rates are not subject to negotiation. NSF Program Officers may not renegotiate cost sharing or other organizational commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget reductions >=10% require scope reduction and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: When discussions result in a budget reduction of 10% or more from the amount originally proposed, a corresponding reduction should be made in the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A revised proposal budget, budget justification, and a Budget Impact Statement describing the impact of the budget reduction on scope must be provided and signed/submitted by the AOR via Research.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Recommendation — program officer role and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: After scientific, technical, and programmatic review and consideration of appropriate factors, the NSF Program Officer recommends to the cognizant NSF Division Director whether the proposal should be declined or recommended for award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recommendation for award does not constitute approval or obligation of Federal funds; only an appointed NSF Grants and Agreements Officer may make commitments or authorize expenditure of funds. Programmatic approval normally occurs at the Division/Office level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to Award — pre-award review and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended proposals go to DGA or DACS for review of business, financial and policy implications; pre-award review includes utilization of NSF’s risk-based framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DGA generally makes the decision to award or decline within 30 days after the program Division/Office makes its recommendation. Major facilities follow Research Infrastructure Guide timelines. Some proposals (e.g., organizations without an active NSF award in last five years, special situations, cooperative agreements, proposals >$20M, or unusual considerations) may require additional review time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting declined proposals to FAPIIS (when applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF will report proposals that are declined for reasons that meet OMB guidelines to the OMB-designated integrity and performance system (currently FAPIIS), but only after the proposer has had an opportunity to exhaust appeal procedures in Chapter III.F.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process to appeal declines for financial or administrative reasons — initial contact
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposer declined for an NSF award for financial or administrative reasons should first discuss the decline decision with the cognizant NSF Grants and Agreements Officer or Branch Chief in DGA or DACS to obtain clarification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This informal discussion is the first step before any formal request for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process to appeal declines — formal request to Division Director (timing & content)
rubrics_metrics.description: If dissatisfied, the proposing organization’s AOR may submit a request for review to the cognizant Division Director of DGA or DACS. The letter must be received by NSF within 30 days after the date of the declination notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request need not follow a prescribed format but must contain a full statement of the proposer’s position, facts and reasons supporting the position, and may include supporting documentation that was available at the time the decline decision was made. New information not available at the time will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process to appeal declines — impartial review and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division Director will review or designate one or more individuals to review the matter; in no case will the review be undertaken by any individual involved with the decline decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing official(s) may request additional information (only that which would have been available at the time the decision was made). Within 30 days of receipt, the reviewer(s) forward a report to the Division Director or designee for a final written decision, which is normally communicated within 15 days of receipt of the report. The Division Director’s decision is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review information provided to PI — what is released
rubrics_metrics.description: When a decision has been made, the following information is released electronically to the PI: description of the process in which the proposal was reviewed; copies of all reviews used in the decision (with any reviewer-identifying information redacted); if reviewed by a panel, a copy of the panel summary and recommendation; and/or site-visit reports, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not otherwise provided in the panel summary, the PI is provided a written explanation of the basis for the declination. A PI may request and obtain any other releasable material in NSF's file on the individual's proposal. Everything in the file, except information that identifies reviewers or other pending or declined proposals, is usually releasable to the PI. Reviews are made available to provide feedback to improve research and proposals and are not intended for any other purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of Recipient Proposal Information — FOIA and exempt material
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal that results in an NSF award will be made available to the public on request, consistent with the Freedom of Information Act, except for privileged information or material that is personal, proprietary, or otherwise exempt from disclosure under law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate labeling in the proposal aids identification of exempt material. Portions of proposals describing inventions in which Government or recipient has rights will not normally be made public until a reasonable time has been allowed for filing patent applications; NSF will notify recipients of requests for copies so recipients may advise NSF of inventions or other confidential/proprietary information.
